results.term_definition: Infrared light is electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths longer than those of visible light but shorter than microwave and radio waves. Infrared light has wavelengths in the range of 700 nanometers to one millimeter while visible light has wavelengths from around 400–700 nanometers. Infrared light is therefore invisible to the human eye and can only be seen with special cameras. Thermal bodies with temperatures of tens to a few thousand kelvins, such as molecular clouds in space, the human body, or brown dwarfs, have their peak electromagnetic emission in infrared light.
